Directions: Based on the passage and illustration below and on your knowledge of social studies, answer each question that follows.
Content: . . . “I started from Cork, by the mail [coach] (says our informant), for Skibbereen and saw little until we came to Clonakilty, where the coach stopped for breakfast; and here, for the `text(first)` time, the horrors of the poverty became visible, in the vast number of famished poor, who flocked around the coach to beg alms: amongst them was a woman carrying in her arms the corpse of a fine child, and making the most distressing appeal to the passengers for aid to enable her to purchase a coffin and bury her dear little baby. This horrible spectacle induced me to make some inquiry about her, when I learned from the people of the hotel that `text(each day)` brings `text(dozens)` of such applicants into the town. . . .”
Copyright: Source: James Mahony, “Sketches in the West of Ireland,” The Illustrated London News, `text(February 13, 1847)` (adapted)
